findings.title: Unguarded dict access on integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise uncaught KeyError
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when an Integration record already exists but no OrganizationIntegration is linked, the code does `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The `sender` key in metadata is only populated when pipeline state happens to include it during build_integration (via `state.get("sender")`), which this PR never binds anywhere in the pipeline; in practice this field appears to rely on an out-of-band webhook updating the integration's metadata after the fact. Any Integration row that was created before this logic existed, or where the corresponding webhook has not yet been processed (a realistic race given webhooks are typically processed asynchronously), will not have a `sender` key in its metadata. Accessing `integration.metadata["sender"]` in that case raises an unhandled KeyError, producing a 500 error for the user instead of the intended graceful 'invalid installation request' page. The code should defensively use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing sender as a failed/ambiguous match (returning `error()`), not crash.

findings.title: Overly broad exception swallowing hides real errors during token exchange
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the code wraps the token-exchange response parsing in a bare `except Exception: payload = {}` with no logging. Any failure here (network error inside safe_urlread, decode error, malformed response, etc.) is silently converted into an empty payload and surfaces only as the generic 'Invalid installation request' error page, with no logged diagnostic information. This makes it difficult to distinguish genuine security failures (bad/reused code, state mismatch) from transient/operational failures (GitHub API outages, encoding issues), hampering debugging and incident response.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 'installation not found' code path
findings.body: The test still mocks a 404 response for `/app/installations/{installation_id}` (used by build_integration to detect a missing GitHub installation), but now sends a 'state' value ('ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05') that does not match the new pipeline.signature check added in OAuthLoginView. As a result, the request now fails earlier at the state-mismatch check in OAuthLoginView.dispatch and never reaches build_integration or the mocked 404 endpoint at all. The assertion was changed from checking 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' to the generic 'Invalid installation request.', meaning the original 404/'installation not found' behavior in build_integration is no longer covered by any test, despite the test name implying it still is.

findings.title: Missing dedicated tests for access_token exchange failure and missing 'login' in user info
findings.body: The PR description explicitly calls out two new failure conditions it intends to guard against: (1) GitHub failing to return a valid access_token (e.g. invalid/reused code) and (2) the authenticated user info lacking a 'login' field. The added test suite (test_github_user_mismatch, test_installation_not_found, etc.) does not directly exercise either of these two branches (lines ~431 and ~435 in integration.py) by mocking a token-exchange response without 'access_token' or a /user response without 'login'. These are core new security-relevant code paths introduced by the PR and should have explicit regression tests.
